fatal_errors: The proposed Y2O3 dispersion intervention does not reconstruct the target intervention of varying Mo content in a Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3-containing CoCrFeNiMox composite.
The starting material is incorrectly treated as cast, unmodified CoCrFeNi rather than the specified powder-processed self-lubricating composite.
No prior evidence is cited for the central claim that Y2O3 will nucleate a continuous, lubricious tribo-oxide film up to 800 °C.
Critical test boundaries—8 N load, Si3N4 counterface, 0.15 m/s speed, 270 m distance, and intermediate temperatures—are omitted.
The assertion that dispersion strengthening will reduce friction as well as wear at low temperature is not adequately justified; increased hardness does not inherently lower interfacial shear.
Testing only room temperature, 400 °C, and 800 °C cannot establish full-range performance or detect the target system's friction maximum near 200 °C.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad engineering problem and offers a single, testable intervention with a control and an explicit rejection criterion. However, it is neither a reconstruction of the target material strategy nor a well-supported alternative. It misses the Mo-dependent lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening, the low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, and the high-temperature silver-molybdate/NiO glaze mechanism. Its predicted uniform improvement also overlooks the important intermediate-temperature deterioration observed in the target system. The proposed experiment has useful microscopy and tribology measurements, but lacks fixed load, speed, counterface, distance, complete temperature sampling, replication details, and any cited evidence establishing that Y2O3 would generate a low-shear tribofilm.
